articles.title: Eleições 2026: veja como foi o dia dos candidatos ao governo da Bahia neste domingo | G1
articles.standfirst: Confira as atividades de campanha de ACM Neto; Jerônimo Rodrigues; Aroldo Felix; Maria Bona; Ariel Capistrano; e Ronaldo Mansur.
articles.summary: Confira as atividades de campanha de ACM Neto; Jerônimo Rodrigues; Aroldo Felix; Maria Bona; Ariel Capistrano; e Ronaldo Mansur.
articles.body:
Candidatos ao governo da Bahia em 2026 — Foto: Reprodução/DivulgaCand

Os candidatos ao governo da Bahia cumpriram compromissos de campanha neste domingo (6). Entre as atividades do dia, estiveram carretas em diversas cidades do interior da Bahia e a presença na 23ª Parada do Orgulho LGBT+ em Salvador .

O candidato do União Brasil participou de carreata em Vitória da Conquista, no sudoeste da Bahia, com a prefeita da cidade, Sheila Lemos (União Brasil); o candidato a vice-governador, Zé Cocá (PP); e os candidatos ao Senado, Angelo Coronel (Republicanos) e João Roma (PL).

O candidato à reeleição pelo PT participou de carretas nas cidades de São Domingos, Valente, Santaluz, Queimadas, Cansanção e Monte Santo, com Jaques Wagner (PT) e Rui Costa, candidatos ao Senado.

O candidato da Unidade Popular participou de uma caminhada no bairro de Itapuã, em Salvador, e teve reunião com famílias do Movimento de Luta nos Bairros, Vilas e Favelas (MLB) em Simões Filho, na Região Metropolitana de Salvador.

A candidata do Partido da Causa Operária não divulgou a agenda até a publicação desta reportagem.

O candidato do Democracia Cristã cumpriu agenda em Salvador neste domingo. Ele participou da Festa de Marujos, em São Joaquim, e fez uma visita comunitária no bairro de Pernambués.

O candidato do PSOL teve reunião com a coordenação de campanha e participou da 23ª Parada do Orgulho LGBT+ Bahia, em Salvador.

articles.title: Em pronunciamento pelo 7 de Setembro, Lula diz que Brasil 'não é colônia' e que decisões pertencem ao país e 'a mais ninguém' | G1
articles.standfirst: Petista fez um discurso de defesa da soberania e críticas indiretas ao tarifaço imposto pelos Estados Unidos a produtos brasileiros. Presidente consultou TSE para transmitir mensagem em rádio e TV.
articles.summary: Petista fez um discurso de defesa da soberania e críticas indiretas ao tarifaço imposto pelos Estados Unidos a produtos brasileiros. Presidente consultou TSE para transmitir mensagem em rádio e TV.
articles.body:
Em pronunciamento pelo 7 de Setembro neste domingo (6), o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) afirmou que o Brasil não é e nem será "colônia de ninguém".

Na mensagem, transmitida em cadeia nacional de rádio e TV, o petista fez um discurso de defesa da soberania e críticas indiretas ao tarifaço imposto pelos Estados Unidos a produtos brasileiros.

"Precisamos nos manter fortes e altivos, sem baixar a cabeça, para não deixarmos que o Brasil se transforme, novamente, em colônia de outras potências estrangeiras. Não somos, e não seremos colônia de ninguém."

Presidente Lula em pronunciamento pelo 7 de Setembro — Foto: Ricardo Stuckert

Lula afirmou que "um país soberano é aquele capaz de defender seu território, suas fronteiras, seu meio ambiente, suas riquezas e seu povo de quaisquer interesses estrangeiros".

"Um país soberano é aquele capaz de criar as oportunidades que seu povo precisa para conquistar a própria independência", disse o presidente.

"Defendemos o livre comércio. Nenhum governante estrangeiro tem o direito de dizer de quem podemos comprar, e para quem podemos vender. Somos um país soberano, e nossas decisões pertencem a nós e a mais ninguém."

No pronunciamento, o presidente Lula também destacou a exploração de terras raras no país e de petróleo na Foz do Amazonas .

O petista citou, ainda, a aprovação no Senado do projeto que cria a Política Nacional de Minerais Críticos e Estratégicos (PNMCE) , com um fundo garantidor para estimular projetos e crédito tributário de R$ 5 bilhões para incentivar o processamento de minérios no país.

"Mais do que nunca, é preciso lutar pelo que é nosso. Temos a segunda maior reserva de Terras Raras do mundo, e a maior fonte de água doce. No último mês, descobrimos uma nova e rica reserva de petróleo. Essas riquezas devem servir ao futuro do povo brasileiro. Foi aprovado no Congresso Nacional o marco legal que permitirá ao Brasil transformar as enormes reservas de minerais críticos e terras raras em desenvolvimento e riqueza para o povo brasileiro", disse.

"Recursos naturais que, assim como o nosso petróleo, devem ser usados para o desenvolvimento de tecnologia de ponta e gerando empregos de qualidade no Brasil."

Para evitar que o pronunciamento fosse questionado na Justiça Eleitoral por ser ano de eleições, a Secretaria de Comunicação Social da Presidência da República solicitou ao TSE autorização para que o petista realizasse a fala em rede nacional.

Na decisão, Nunes Marques afirma que a divulgação do pronunciamento "é de interesse público".

"Na medida em que a data integra o calendário oficial brasileiro e possui significado histórico e institucional autônomo em relação às funções de governo e, especialmente, às atribuições institucionais de Chefia de Estado", escreveu Nunes Marques.

articles.title: Reformas em sepulturas podem ser feitas até 23 de outubro em Prudente | G1
articles.standfirst: Serviços devem ser concluídos antes da suspensão temporária das obras para a preparação dos cemitérios para o Dia de Finados, celebrado em 2 de novembro.
articles.summary: Os moradores que pretendem realizar reformas ou reparos em sepulturas nos cemitérios municipais de Presidente Prudente (SP) devem ficar atentos ao prazo.
articles.body:
Cemitério Municipal São João Batista em Presidente Prudente (SP) — Foto: Arquivo/g1

Os moradores que pretendem realizar reformas ou reparos em sepulturas nos cemitérios municipais de Presidente Prudente (SP) devem ficar atentos ao prazo. Os serviços podem ser realizados até o dia 23 de outubro.

Até a data, estão autorizadas intervenções como construções, aplicação de revestimentos, pinturas e reparos nas sepulturas.

Após o prazo, serão permitidos somente serviços de lavagem dos túmulos e polimento de peças de bronze.

A suspensão temporária das obras faz parte da preparação dos cemitérios municipais para o Dia de Finados, celebrado em 2 de novembro.

No período que antecede a data, as equipes intensificam os trabalhos de limpeza, manutenção e organização dos espaços para receber os visitantes.

A expectativa é de grande movimentação nos dois cemitérios municipais durante o Dia de Finados. No Cemitério Municipal São João Batista, são esperadas aproximadamente 20 mil pessoas. Já no Cemitério Campal, a previsão é de cerca de 8 mil visitantes.

A orientação da Prefeitura é para que as famílias que pretendem realizar reformas ou reparos se programem para concluir os serviços dentro do prazo estabelecido.

Para mais informações, os moradores podem entrar em contato diretamente com as administrações dos cemitérios. O telefone do Cemitério Municipal São João Batista é (18) 3908-3644. Para o Cemitério Campal, o atendimento é pelo telefone (18) 3909-2244.

articles.title: Mendonça libera para plenário do STF caso de mensagens entre Moraes e Vorcaro; decisão cabe a Fachin | G1
articles.standfirst: Caberá ao presidente da Corte decidir quando e se caso será analisado pelo plenário. E ainda o modelo: sessão aberta ou fechada. PGR alegou nulidades na decisão de Mendonça sobre tema.
articles.summary: Caberá ao presidente da Corte decidir quando e se caso será analisado pelo plenário. E ainda o modelo: sessão aberta ou fechada. PGR alegou nulidades na decisão de Mendonça sobre tema.
articles.body:
O ministro André Mendonça , do Supremo Tribunal Federal, liberou neste domingo (6) para julgamento no plenário da Corte o relatório da Polícia Federal que apontou uma suposta relação entre o ministro Alexandre de Moraes e o ex-banqueiro Daniel Vorcaro.

Agora, cabe ao presidente do STF, ministro Edson Fachin, decidir o que fazer, portanto, quando e se o caso será analisado pelo plenário. E ainda o modelo: sessão aberta ou fechada.

Fachin deve aguardar as respostas dos ministros do tribunal André Mendonça e Alexandre de Moraes, do procurador-geral da República (PGR), Paulo Gonet , e do diretor-geral da Polícia Federal, Andrei Rodrigues, para se manifestar. O presidente do STF deu até sexta-feira (11) para que eles prestem informações sobre os acontecimentos que causaram uma crise no STF.

⚖️ No caso de optar pelo plenário, Fachin ainda precisa definir se será uma sessão aberta ou fechada. Os ministros decidirão então se abrem investigação ou se arquivam as apurações que implicam Moraes.

⚖️ Fachin pode decidir ainda por uma reunião reservada, como ocorreu em fevereiro, quando outro relatório da PF mostrou troca de mensagens entre o ministro Dias Toffoli e o ex-dono do Banco Master.

⚖️ Há ainda a possibilidade de o ministro Fachin decidir de forma individual se abre ou arquiva o relatório. Essa alternativa é considerada, por pessoas ouvidas pela reportagem, mais remota.

Na imagem, ministros do STF: Alexandre de Moraes (dir.) e André Mendonça — Foto: Fotos de: Fabio Rodrigues-Pozzebom da Agência Brasil e Carlos Moura do STF

A indicação é de que Fachin teria preferência por uma sessão pública, mas que o modelo só deve ser confirmado após uma consulta que vem fazendo aos colegas.

Como mostrou o blog do jornalista Valdo Cruz, Fachin sinalizou ao presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) que pretende levar ao plenário da Corte os desdobramentos da crise envolvendo os ministros Alexandre de Moraes e André Mendonça.

A avaliação é que as acusações e questionamentos que vieram à tona nos últimos dias precisam ser analisados pelo conjunto dos ministros, e não apenas por meio de decisões individuais. Fachin também demonstrou incômodo com a forma como os dois lados vêm conduzindo o embate.

⚖️ O regimento do STF não trata especificamente sobre como uma investigação contra um ministro deve ser conduzida. O documento diz apenas que compete ao plenário processar e julgar.

Em discurso nessa sexta-feira (4) em evento no Palácio do Planalto, o presidente do STF afirmou que nenhuma autoridade está acima da Constituição e que resposta a fatos "graves" será "firme".

Ele também afirmou que a "gravidade" dos acontecimentos tornados públicos na semana passada – que envolvem relações do banqueiro Daniel Vorcaro com ministros da Corte e com o procurador-geral da República, Paulo Gonet, e a atuação de magistrados – "não autoriza atalhos".

PGR se manifestou pela nulidade da investigação

O Procurador-Geral da República Paulo Gonet — Foto: Victor Piemonte/STF

A PGR argumentou que o ministro André Mendonça não deveria ter solicitado apuração sobre o destinatário das mensagens do ex-banqueiro, sem um pedido do Ministério Público ou da própria PF, e que a competência para decidir sobre a eventual apuração sobre Moraes é do plenário da Corte.

Mendonça defendeu a análise pelo plenário do STF, argumentando que , "diante do teor das informações apresentadas", o caminho inevitável seria a avaliação pelo colegiado, já que é "instância soberana para analisar, de modo técnico e estritamente jurídico".

O advogado Ciro Soares aparece como principal interlocutor entre os dois. Ele foi um dos advogados que impetraram habeas corpus no Superior Tribunal de Justiça (STJ) para tentar reverter a primeira decisão que autorizou a prisão preventiva de Vorcaro.

O presidente do STF, Edson Fachin, afirmou ser necessário colher informações dos ministros do tribunal André Mendonça e Alexandre de Moraes, do procurador-geral da República (PGR), Paulo Gonet, e do diretor-geral da Polícia Federal, Andrei Rodrigues sobre:

o cumprimento pela PF das regras estabelecidas na Lei Orgânica da Magistratura em relação a autoridades com foro no STF;

"indícios de que credenciais de acesso institucional tenham sido utilizadas para avaliar documento estritamente particular e de que informações sujeitas ao sigilo judicial foram reveladas a pessoa investigada";

as circunstâncias em que o ministro Mendonça determinou a identificação de pessoas mencionadas nas investigações do caso Master; e

as medidas tomadas para o controle externo da atividade policial.

Na petição, Moraes disse que há presença de fortes indícios da prática de improbidade administrativa, abuso de autoridade, crime de responsabilidade e favorecimento a determinados grupos políticos no exercício da relatoria dos casos Master e INSS.

A decisão de Moraes foi tomada no âmbito do inquérito das fake news.

articles.title: Tusk: Only 'idiots or traitors' in Poland should celebrate AfD win
articles.summary: Only "idiots or traitors" in Poland should be celebrating the victory for the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) in the eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt,...
articles.body:
Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk criticizes celebration of far-right AfD victory in Saxony-Anhalt, Germany.

AfD narrowly misses absolute majority in state parliament, claims mandate to govern.

Reaction to AfD victory in Saxony-Anhalt varies, with support from Austrian and Czech politicians.

Only "idiots or traitors" in Poland should be celebrating the victory for the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) in the eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt, Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said on Sunday.

The latest projections show the AfD on 44%, narrowly missing out on an absolute majority of seats in the state parliament in Magdeburg. However, the party has claimed a mandate to govern the state.

"In Poland, only idiots or traitors can rejoice at the triumph of the AfD in Germany," Tusk wrote.

He said that "quite a few" have gathered in two opposition Polish parties - Confederation, and the former governing party Law and Justice (PiS).

Reaction to the AfD's victory was more sympathetic elsewhere in Germany's neighbouring countries.

The leader of the right-wing Freedom Party of Austria (FPÖ), Herbert Kickl, described the result as a sign of political upheaval in Germany.

"From today, the powerful wind of freedom from 1989 is blowing through Germany once again," said Kickl, drawing a comparison with the fall of the Berlin Wall.

Voters in Saxony-Anhalt have torn down the "undemocratic firewall" against the AfD, according to Kickl. The FPÖ is Austria's largest party in parliament, but remains in opposition.

Kickl said the AfD will "ultimately achieve its definitive breakthrough with Alice Weidel as Chancellor", said Kickl, referring to the party's national co-leader.

In the Czech Republic, Parliament Speaker Tomio Okamura congratulated the AfD on its election success on public broadcasting channel CT.

"Above all, I hope that it will form part of the new governing coalition in the federal state of Saxony-Anhalt," said Okamura, whose Freedom and Direct Democracy party is part of Prime Minister Andrej Babiš's government.

images.caption: FILE PHOTO - Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk, speaks during a press conference. (is associated with: «Tusk: Only 'idiots or traitors' in Poland should celebrate AfD win») Bernd von Jutrczenka/dpa

articles.title: Assailant lunged at Democratic candidate for Ohio governor at fair, campaign says
articles.summary: An armed assailant lunged at the Democratic candidate for Ohio governor, Amy Acton, on Sunday during a campaign stop at the Canfield Fair, injuring several p...
articles.body:
WASHINGTON (AP) — An armed assailant lunged at the Democratic candidate for Ohio governor, Amy Acton , on Sunday during a campaign stop at the Canfield Fair, injuring several people, campaign officials said.

The suspect knocked volunteers to the ground and was arrested with "multiple weapons," Mahoning County Democratic Party chairman Chris Anderson said in a statement.

Acton, the state's former public health director, was not injured, but her campaign said multiple people were hurt.

"Dr. Acton will always stand up to the chaos, hate and vitriol that pits us against one another," said Addie Bullock, communications director for the campaign.

Ohio State Highway Patrol and other authorities at the fair quickly responded "when a man tried to forcefully push himself toward Dr. Acton as she was speaking and injured other attendees at the Mahoning County Democrat booth," Republican Gov. Mike DeWine said in a statement.

"Violence or the threat of violence at political or public events is always unacceptable," he added.

The attempted attack is the latest political violence to roil the United States. And the Ohio gubernatorial race is one of the most high-profile races this year as the campaigns enter the final six weeks of campaigning before the election in November.

Acton is facing Republican Vivek Ramaswamy , who has parlayed his national name recognition, tech industry connections and alliance with President Donald Trump into a record fundraising haul that he is tapping for advertising spots aimed at the November election. He is using campaign rallies and advertising to criticize Acton.

Ramaswamy's campaign called the incident Sunday unacceptable.

"Candidates should be able to meet with voters without having to worry about threats or violence. What happened today is completely unacceptable and has no place in politics, and we hope hope that no one was hurt," Ramaswamy's communications director, Connie Luck, said in a statement.

The fairground's police department referred inquiries to the Mahoning County Sheriff's Department, which didn't immediately return a message seeking comment. The Ohio State Highway Patrol didn't immediately respond to a request for information.

The incident brought condemnation from Ohio Republican Sen. John Husted, who said on X that he and his wife were "disturbed by the attempted attack on Amy Acton today at the Canfield Fair. We are grateful for law enforcement's quick response. There is no place for this kind of behavior, and it must never be tolerated."

The country has seen a rise in political violence over the past decade . That includes the 2017 shooting at a Republican congressional baseball team practice in Alexandria, Virginia; the 2022 hammer assault on the husband of Democratic then-House Speaker Nancy Pelosi in California; the 2024 assassination attempt on Donald Trump at a Pennsylvania rally during his presidential campaign as well as another on the president at this year's White House Correspondents' Association Dinner in April; and the assassinations last year of a Democratic Minnesota state lawmaker and her husband and of conservative commentator Charlie Kirk in Utah.

Federal political committees spent more than $40 million on expenses labeled as security during the 2023-24 campaign cycle, the most recent one for which data is publicly available, according a report released in April from the Public Service Alliance, a nonpartisan group that focuses on security for public officials.

Before running for governor, Acton had been recruited by DeWine in 2019 to lead the Ohio Department of Health while serving as an associate professor of public health at Ohio State University. As the COVID-19 pandemic ramped up in early 2020, she was thrown into the state and national spotlight — becoming a source of comfort to many viewers of the governor's daily news conferences.

For her service as health director, Acton earned the John F. Kennedy Library Foundation's Profile in COVID Courage Award, the Columbus Foundation's Spirit of Columbus Award and Ohio State's highest alumni honor, the Alumni Medalist Award.

Her position as the face of the DeWine administration's aggressive stance against the virus also earned Acton many enemies, among them Statehouse Republicans and average Ohioans who opposed pandemic restrictions.

Associated Press writer Ryan J. Foley in Iowa City, Iowa, contributed to this report.

images.caption: FILE - Democratic gubernatorial candidate Dr. Amy Acton speaks at a primary election night campaign event after winning the party's nomination for governor on May 5, 2026, in Columbus, Ohio. (AP Photo/Jay LaPrete, File)

articles.title: Germany's AfD Is Not 'Far Right'
articles.body:
Germany's Alternative for Germany (AfD) party has seen significant electoral success, winning 44% of the vote in the recent state election in Saxony-Anhalt.

The AfD's policy positions include advocating for stricter immigration controls, a rollback of European integration, and a return to nuclear power in Germany.

The party's rise is attributed to dissatisfaction with left-wing policies, particularly in areas such as energy, climate, and immigration, and it has become the second-largest parliamentary bloc in the Bundestag.

This week I predicted that Germany's Alternative for Germany would likely win Sunday's state election in Saxony-Anhalt, a development I called "earth-shattering."

The AfD has now moved from a protest party on the margins to one capable of winning elections outright.

It is important to note that the party is not "far right" — as much of the European and international press labels it.

Such labels have been a clever way for the left-wing press, which itself has become increasingly radically left (think claims there are more than biological sexes), to redefine the center in its favor.

With Germany's press largely on the left and without an outlet comparable to Newsmax or Fox, the AfD's success is even more significant.

The public is seeing through the media manipulation.

The AfD is clearly conservative and rightist, but also populist and nationalist.

Founded in 2013 primarily as a Eurosceptic response to the eurozone crisis, the AfD shifted substantially toward nationalism, immigration, and cultural issues during and after the 2015 refugee crisis.

All of these are reasonable political positions to hold.

Europe just 10 years ago had 24% of the world's GDP. Today, it has just 16%.

This is an economic catastrophe brought about by left-wing socialism that embraced climate change and "net zero" policies that destroyed economic growth.

Germany has particularly suffered. Notably, then-Chancellor Angela Merkel accelerated Germany's nuclear phaseout after the Fukushima disaster.

In the February 2025 federal election, the AfD won 20.8% of the party-list vote, roughly double its 2021 result.

It secured 152 of the Bundestag's 630 seats, up from 83, making it the second-largest parliamentary bloc behind the CDU/CSU.

The party remains significantly stronger in the former East Germany. Recent polling had it around 40% in several eastern states, including about 41% in Saxony-Anhalt.

Today's Saxony-Anhalt election represents a new breakthrough. Early projections put the AfD at more than 44%.

The AfD's policy positions are conservative and, again, reasonable. Here is a rundown of its key positions:

Immigration and asylum are probably the party's defining issues.

Its 2025 federal platform calls for permanent border controls, turning away unauthorized entrants, processing asylum applications outside Germany, and what it calls the "remigration" of people without a legal right to remain.

It also advocates German withdrawal from the U.N. migration and refugee compacts.

On the European Union, the AfD wants a fundamental rollback of European integration.

Its 2025 program calls for replacing today's increasingly integrated EU with a looser association of sovereign nations and an economic community.

It opposes the EU Green Deal, fiscal transfers, and a digital euro. The party's underlying principle is that substantially more authority should return from Brussels to national governments.

On Russia and Ukraine, it diverges sharply from Germany's mainstream parties. The AfD calls for ending economic sanctions against Russia, restoring normal trade, and repairing the Nord Stream pipelines.

Its federal manifesto says Ukraine should remain outside both NATO and the European Union as a neutral state.

This makes an AfD breakthrough relevant beyond German domestic politics: A national government dependent on the party could substantially alter Berlin's approach toward Ukraine, Russia, NATO, and European security.

Energy and climate policy are another major dividing line.

The AfD wants Germany to return to nuclear power, expand or retain coal generation, eliminate the CO2 levy, and end renewable-energy subsidies.

It portrays Germany's energy transition and EU climate regulation as threats to industrial competitiveness and household living standards.

Economically, the party mixes market-oriented policies with economic nationalism.

It favors lower taxes, deregulation, simplification of the tax system, abolition of the solidarity surcharge, and policies designed to strengthen small and medium-sized German businesses.

Its economic message increasingly links taxation, energy prices, EU regulation, and immigration to the broader claim that established governments have undermined German prosperity.

On social and family policy, the AfD favors a more traditional conception of family. Its federal program advocates family income splitting for taxation, allowances for parents caring for young children, and other financial incentives intended to increase Germany's birth rate.

On crime and policing, it calls for more police personnel and equipment, tougher penalties and investigative powers against terrorism, extremism, gangs, and organized crime, and greater confiscation of criminal assets. These positions are closely integrated with its immigration message.

On media and political institutions, the party advocates a major overhaul of Germany's public broadcasting system, arguing that it should become considerably smaller and focus on information and culture.

It also has a longstanding commitment to more Swiss-style direct democracy and national referendums.

The AfD's rise has entered a new phase — from disrupting Germany's party system to potentially governing parts of it.

Today's election in Saxony-Anhalt shows again that nothing is more powerful than an idea — or a party — whose time has come.

John Gizzi is chief political columnist and White House correspondent for Newsmax. For more of his reports, Go Here Now.

articles.title: Amy Acton campaign says armed individual lunged at Ohio governor candidate, injuring multiple people
articles.summary: Amy Acton's campaign says the Ohio governor candidate was targeted by an armed individual at the Canfield Fair as political violence fears mount.
articles.body: An armed individual lunged at Ohio gubernatorial candidate Amy Acton and injured multiple people Sunday in a burst of violence at the Canfield Fair, her campaign said. "While attending the Canfield Fair, an armed individual lunged at Dr. Acton, injuring multiple people," Acton campaign communications director Addie Bullock said in a statement. "Dr. Acton and Eric are grateful for the swift and decisive action of law enforcement and are praying for the recovery of those injured," Bullock added. "This kind of violence has no place in Ohio. Dr. Acton will always stand up to the chaos, hate and vitriol that pits us against one another." TRUMP'S DECADE OF ASSASSINATION THREATS RUNS FROM BUTLER SHOOTING TO LATEST GOLF CLUB BREACH Ohio Gov. Mike DeWine later confirmed that Acton was not hurt and said he and first lady Fran DeWine spoke with her following the incident. "Fran and I are thankful Dr. Amy Acton was not hurt, and we send our thoughts to those who were injured," DeWine said. "We spoke to Dr. Acton this afternoon and she said to share with Ohioans that she is ok." DeWine said a man "tried to forcefully push himself toward Dr. Acton" as she was speaking and injured other attendees at the Mahoning County Democratic booth. "We are grateful for the quick work of the Ohio State Highway Patrol and other law enforcement on the scene at the Canfield Fair today," the governor said. "Violence or the threat of violence at political or public events is always unacceptable," DeWine added. "This case is now in the hands of law enforcement and will be investigated thoroughly." Officials did not immediately identify the man or say whether he had been arrested. Acton’s campaign described him as armed, although DeWine did not mention a weapon. The conditions of those injured were also unclear. It was also unclear what prompted the confrontation and whether anyone had been arrested. The incident came as Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin warned that candidates and other public figures continue to face threats as campaign season kicks into high gear. "You’re never safe in the public eye," Mullin told Fox News’ Peter Doocy during an interview on "The Sunday Briefing." WHITE HOUSE CORRESPONDENTS’ DINNER SHOOTING LATEST IN YEARS OF ATTACKS TARGETING TRUMP, CONSERVATIVES Doocy asked Mullin whether candidates were safe heading into the traditional Labor Day weekend kickoff to campaign season, citing the political assassinations and assassination attempts that have rocked the country in recent years. "If you read any of the social media posts, which I choose not to, but you see the type of rhetoric and the hatefulness that’s out there," Mullin said. DEM SENATE HOPEFULS UNDER SCRUTINY FOR ‘CHOKE THEM OUT’ RHETORIC AFTER TRUMP ATTACK SCARE "The threats to our elected officials, they don’t go away," he continued. "We’ve got to bring down the temperature, but the temperature is not going to go down on itself." Mullin said Americans must accept that political disagreements are part of the country’s system of government while drawing a firm line at violence. WEST VIRGINIA MAN PLEADS GUILTY TO MAKING VIOLENT THREATS AGAINST TRUMP, ICE "The American people have to realize that we do have a republic, and the republic has different opinions, and it’s OK to have different opinions," he said. "When you cross a line and say that that different opinion needs to be silenced — it needs to be silenced through violence — that’s where Homeland comes into place," Mullin added. "Free speech is something we all protect, but there’s a line that you can cross that goes from free speech to inciting dangerous behavior." Mullin was speaking broadly about political threats and was not responding directly to the reported confrontation involving Acton. Republican gubernatorial nominee Vivek Ramaswamy and his running mate, Ohio Senate President Rob McColley, condemned the Canfield Fair incident. "Candidates should be able to meet with voters without having to worry about threats or violence," Ramaswamy campaign communications director Connie Luck said in a statement. "What happened today is completely unacceptable and has no place in politics, and we hope that no one was hurt," she added. RAMASWAMY OUTLINES KEY CONTRASTS WITH DEM OPPONENT LESS THAN 100 DAYS OUT FROM KEY GUBERNATORIAL ELECTION Acton and Ramaswamy are facing off in November’s closely watched race to replace term-limited Republican Gov. Mike DeWine. Acton, a physician, became a household name in Ohio while serving as director of the Ohio Department of Health during the COVID-19 pandemic, according to The Associated Press. She appeared alongside DeWine during televised briefings as the state imposed shutdowns and other public-health restrictions. Her handling of the pandemic has since become a central campaign issue, The AP reported. Ramaswamy and other Republicans have criticized Acton over the restrictions, while her campaign has defended her work with DeWine as necessary to protect Ohioans. articles.title: Trump posts map labeling New Mexico as ‘New America’ after online hoax
articles.summary: President Trump on Sunday posted a map of New Mexico labeled “New America” following the spread of a since-debunked online hoax claiming he had signed an executive order renaming the state. The map Trump shared on Truth Social showed a large “X” over “Mexico” in the state’s name, with the word “America” labeled below it.…
articles.body:
President Trump on Sunday posted a map of New Mexico labeled “New America” following the spread of a since-debunked online hoax claiming he had signed an executive order renaming the state.

The map Trump shared on Truth Social showed a large “X” over “Mexico” in the state’s name, with the word “America” labeled below it. The official White House account reposted the image to social platform X.

Fact-checking website Snopes detailed how an X user posted the “New America” executive order claim on Sept. 1, going viral across other social media platforms. The outlet debunked the report , noting the original post came from a satirical social media account.

The hoax followed the president’s recent order to rename Lake Ontario “Lake America” amid his trade war with Canada.

Lawmakers chimed in after Trump shared his Sunday post, with Democrats denouncing the notion of renaming a state. Many noted the move would be in line with the president’s past orders renaming landmarks — including the Great Lake name change and last year’s order changing the Gulf of Mexico to the “Gulf of America.”

“Three things I will always call by their actual names,” Sen. Martin Heinrich (D-N.M.) wrote on X . “The Gulf of Mexico. Lake Ontario. New Mexico.”

Rep. Melanie Stansbury (D-N.M.) said separately, “Oh hell no!”

“Our state’s name carries generations of history, culture, and family — and it belongs to us,” she wrote on X . “We’re New Mexicans. Period.”

Rep. Gabe Vasquez (D-N.M.), who is running for reelection against Republican Greg Cunningham, told the president on X that he doesn’t “get to erase New Mexico. Not our name. Not our history. Not our culture.”

“The President may want to call us ‘ New America, ‘ but we know who we are,” he added.

Rep. Ted Lieu (D-Calif.) responded by citing the increase in gas and diesel prices seen over the course of the Iran war before asking what Trump and GOP lawmakers are “focused on.”

“Changing the name of New Mexico to New America,” Lieu answered himself. “November is coming.”

At least one GOP lawmaker reacted to the post . Sen. Mike Lee (R-Utah) said “New America” was “kind of catchy.”

Trump’s renaming of other bodies of water largely drew criticism, including from Mexican and Canadian officials, respectively. Mexico’s government sued Google last year after it changed the name of the Gulf of Mexico on its Maps platform, with Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum accusing the company of violating her country’s sovereignty.

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said Lake Ontario’s name still applied to “Canadians and the rest of the world. Now and forever.” He referred to its ties to indigenous history and culture, named after the Wendat word for “the lake is beautiful, the lake is big.”

The Seneca Nation — one of the six nations of the Haudenosaunee, or Iroquois, Confederacy — urged Trump to reverse the order. They said the name change violated the terms of the 1794 Treaty of Canandaigua , which states the boundaries for the Seneca people are specified as “beginning on Lake Ontario.” Leaders of the Haudenosaunee and former President George Washington signed the treaty.

House Democrats last week introduced legislation attempting to block Trump’s Lake America order, as well as prevent the president and his administration from renaming other Great Lakes.

Rep. Claudia Tenney (R-N.Y.) — whose district covers much of Lake Ontario’s shoreline — told TMZ she was “pretty sure” Trump’s executive order was just “a troll” against Canada.

articles.title: Trump appears to debut darker hair, sparking online buzz
articles.summary: New photos of President Trump stepping off Air Force One with what appeared to be a darker hairstyle have quickly fueled social media buzz.
articles.body: President Donald Trump appeared to debut a darker hair color Friday, sparking widespread speculation online after stepping off Air Force One in New Jersey ahead of a weekend at his Bedminster golf club. Known for his signature blond hairstyle, Trump was photographed arriving at Morristown Municipal Airport with what appeared to be a noticeably darker, more brunette look —prompting a flood of reactions across social media. "Trump becoming a brunette was definitely not on my 2026 bingo card," one user wrote on X. "This was Donald Trump yesterday while departing to New Jersey for the weekend! Look at the appearance of his hair! Is he getting a new hair color?" another user wrote. HOUSE DEMS PLOT TRUMP INVESTIGATION BLITZ IF THEY SEIZE MAJORITY "Seems brown is the new blonde ...," a third user added. "Trump is now a brunette!" another post read. Photos shared on Instagram by internet personality Michael Solakiewicz showed Trump golfing Saturday in a red hat that covered most of his hair, making it difficult to tell whether the darker look remained. TRUMP’S PENTAGON SHAKE-UP REVIVES A PRESIDENTIAL POWER PLAY WITH A LONG HISTORY The online speculation comes just days after Trump pushed back on allegations that he wears a wig, pointing to a windy 2024 campaign rally in Ohio, according to The Hill. "I don’t wear a wig. But that night, they found out I did not wear a wig because if you did, it was not going to be on your head very long," Trump said Wednesday. Trump has rarely made noticeable changes to his appearance while in office. TRUMP NEGOTIATORS WITKOFF, KUSHNER MEET WITH PUTIN IN MOSCOW AS US PUSHES FOR END TO RUSSIA-UKRAINE WAR CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP In 2019, he sparked similar speculation after appearing with what looked like a slicked-back hairstyle during a surprise visit to a Virginia church. That hairstyle was short-lived. Trump spoke to reporters later in the day wearing his usual hairdo. The White House could not immediately be reached by Fox News Digital for comment. Fox News Digital's Bradford Betz contributed to this report.
